fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The verse says Hamath and Arpad are put to shame “…for they have heard a bad report…” The report is the reason the verse gives. Some news lands harder than a dropped tray of cookies.
Fire it is. The LORD says, “I will set fire to the walls of Damascus; it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.” Fire in my bakery is the oven's job, and it stays in the oven.
No locusts here, baker. The verse says “I will set fire to the walls of Damascus…” The word that fits the blank is fire, not locusts.

Cyrus, king of Persia, is a real king in the Bible (Ezra 1:1). But this verse names someone else. It says Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor were defeated by “…Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…” Right king, but he's not the one in this verse, friend.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has drawn up a plan against you; he has devised a strategy against you.” That's the reason given. Right before it, the LORD tells Hazor, “Run! Escape quickly! Lie low…”

The text says the opposite, friend. This nation is one that “dwells securely,” and then the verse says, “They have no gates or bars; they live alone.” So gates and bars aren't part of this picture. Dwelling securely and having gates turn out to be two different things.
That's right. The LORD says, “I will bring calamity on them from all sides…” The verse doesn't name one direction. It says all sides.
That's the one. The LORD says, “Hazor will become a haunt for jackals, a desolation forever.” Then He adds, “No one will dwell there; no man will abide there.”

Winds is it. The LORD says, “I will bring the four winds against Elam from the four corners of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds.” Then He says, “There will not be a nation to which Elam’s exiles will not go.”

Plagues don't appear in this verse, friend. The LORD says He will bring “…the four winds against Elam from the four corners of the heavens…” So winds is the word that fits the blank. After that He says, “I will scatter them to all these winds.”

His throne, baker. The LORD says He will “destroy its king and officials,” and in the same breath He says, “I will set My throne in Elam…” A throne is the seat of a king, so this is the LORD placing His own seat in Elam.

No altar in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “I will set My throne in Elam, and destroy its king and officials…” A throne is the seat of a king, so the verse puts His own seat in Elam. Altar isn't a word this verse uses.

A banner isn't mentioned, baker. The verse says, “I will set My throne in Elam…” and in the same breath says He will “…destroy its king and officials…” A banner would be a flag, but a throne is a king's seat, and that's what the LORD says He will set there.
